title: Automation
description: A recurring job on a site (RFC-0008), created by a person in Studio: either a built-in deterministic job that Cloudhal runs itself (reports, findings and notifications; it never publishes), or a scheduled agent task that an external agent picks up over MCP with the automation's own key, inside a run window, under a mode cap and budgets. No language model runs inside Cloudhal. Scheduling never grants rights: every call of a task runs with the key's scopes narrowed to its owner's current role. Automations live in D1 next to the graph; they are not graph nodes and are not part of site bundles.

pausedReason.description: Why the automation is not `active`: a person paused it; its agent paused it; three consecutive failures; a run exceeded its budget; the site's kill switch; its key was revoked; its owner left or no longer holds the scopes it needs.

AutomationId.description: An automation id: `aut_` and 6 to 32 letters or digits.

AutomationState.description: `active` runs on its recurrence; `paused` and `auto-paused` (by failures or a budget) wait for a person to resume; `broken` needs a person to repair it (key revoked, owner gone); `ended` reached its COUNT or UNTIL.

AutomationOwner.description: The person who created the automation and owns its key (`user_…`). Agents never own automations.

AutomationRule.description: The recurrence as an RFC 5545 RRULE value in Cloudhal's subset, without the `RRULE:` prefix: FREQ DAILY, WEEKLY or MONTHLY; INTERVAL; BYDAY (ordinals such as 2TU or -1FR only with MONTHLY); BYMONTHDAY (1–31 or -1); BYHOUR; BYMINUTE; COUNT or UNTIL. The pattern bounds the vocabulary; the parser refuses repeated parts, COUNT with UNTIL, ordinals outside MONTHLY and runs closer than the job's minimum interval.

AutomationRecurrence.description: When the automation runs: the first occurrence as a wall-clock time in `timeZone`, repeated by `rule` (absent: once). Occurrences are computed in the zone, so "Mondays 09:07" stays 09:07 across daylight-saving changes; a time that does not exist on a given day (a spring-forward gap) runs at the next valid minute, and a time that occurs twice runs once, at the first (a documented deviation from RFC 5545 §3.3.10, which drops such occurrences). `preset` records which Studio choice produced the rule.

AutomationBudget.description: Per-run limits Cloudhal counts and enforces for an agent task: tool calls, mutations, approval requests filed and minutes since the run began. Exceeding one ends the run (`budget-exceeded`) and pauses the automation.

oneOf.title: BuiltinAutomationJob
oneOf.description: A deterministic job Cloudhal runs itself, in bounded steps. Its outputs are findings, reports and Studio notifications; it never changes or publishes content.

staleAfterDays.description: `stale-content` only: entries not updated for this many days are listed for review.

oneOf.title: AgentTaskAutomationJob
oneOf.description: A task an external agent performs over MCP. At each occurrence a run window opens for `windowMinutes`; the automation's key (`keyId`, owned by the automation's owner) is valid only inside an open run, which the agent starts with `begin_run` and ends with `end_run`. The run's mode is the key's effective mode capped by `modeCap`; it never waits for a person: calls that need one leave an approval request and the run ends. `readsUntrustedText` declares that the task reads visitor-supplied text (comments, 404 paths, fetched pages); such an automation's key cannot hold write scopes, and any run that reads such text is limited to reading, labelling and hiding from then on.

instructions.description: What the owner asks the agent to do, shown to the agent by `begin_run`. Plain text.

skill.description: A skill the run declares (its scopes and approval list narrow the run further).

modeCap.description: The most autonomous mode a run may use; never `bypass`.
